mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.5% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as borrowing costs rise and economic activity slows.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between FEDFUNDS increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in real GDP (more than 1% quarter-over-quarter) indicates a weakening economy, which typically results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as corporate earnings expectations decline.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between GDP decline and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (more than 0.5% in one month) signals labor market weakness, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer spending and business confidence decline.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between UNRATE increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in industrial production (more than 2% month-over-month) signals a strong supply side, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as market sentiment improves.
failure_condition: If the 5-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between INDPRO increase and positive returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of rising housing starts and retail sales signals strong consumer demand, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as consumer-driven sectors outperform.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are negative in more than 40% of the instances where both proxies are increasing, or if the joint effect of HOUST and RSAFS on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: An increase in nonfarm payrolls combined with a decrease in the unemployment rate signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer spending and business investment increase.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances where both proxies move in the predicted direction, or if the joint effect of PAYEMS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in the Consumer Price Index (more than 0.5% month-over-month) signals inflationary pressure, which typically leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as real returns are eroded and the Fed is expected to tighten monetary policy.
failure_condition: If the 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of the instances where the trigger condition is met, or if the correlation between CPIAUCSL increase and negative returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A combination of a significant increase in retail sales and a decrease in the unemployment rate signals robust consumer demand and a strong labor market, which typically leads to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as consumer-driven sectors outperform.
failure_condition: If the 60-day forward returns are negative in more than 30% of the instances where both proxies move in the predicted direction, or if the joint effect of RSAFS and UNRATE on returns is not statistically significant (p > 0.05).
